AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Little research has been expended on the use of bipolar radiofrequency (RF) lesioning of sacral nerves in spinal cord injured (SCI) patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO), and no study has been undertaken to demonstrate its long-term effect.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To investigated the effect of bipolar RF ablation of the second and third sacral nerves over 2 years in SCI patients with NDO.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A prospective, randomized controlled feasibility study.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: The outpatient clinic of a single academic medical center in Korea.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Ten SCI patients with NDO were recruited. These patients were randomly assigned to 2 groups; the intervention group (n = 5) and the control group (n = 5). Control group members received optimized conventional treatment. International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ), 3-day voiding diary, and the urinary incontinence quality of life scale (I-QOL) data were obtained at baseline and at 6, 12, and 24 months after intervention. Urodynamic study (UDS) was performed at baseline and 24 months after intervention. In the intervention group, percutaneous bipolar RF neurotomy was performed on both S2 and S3 nerves in each patient.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Frequency of urinary incontinence and ICIQ and IQOL scores showed significant effects for time and for the group x time interaction (P < 0.05). Daily mean volume of urinary incontinence showed only a significant group effect. In UDS parameters, comparisons of values at baseline and at 24 months revealed all variables showed significant intergroup differences (P < 0.05).

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATION
AbstractText.content: A small number of patients was recruited.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Percutaneous bipolar RF ablation of sacral nerves S2 and S3 effectively reduces urinary incontinence and improves quality of life (QoL) in SCI patients with NDO and the effects lasted over 2 years.
